questions.question: You could be known for one extraordinary talent. What would you choose?

answers.text: Being exceptionally powerful at one thing.
Leading a big group that gets better together.
Combining unrelated skills into something surprising.
Seeing problems coming and deciding how situations unfold.

questions.question: You are planning a weekend with friends. Rank what you would focus on first.

answers.text: Get things moving and make plans right away.
Work out a reliable plan with plenty to do.
Anticipate problems and prepare alternatives.
Plan one unforgettable surprise as the highlight.

questions.question: How satisfying is it to watch something you built gradually grow stronger?
A project you cared about unexpectedly falls apart. What would be the most satisfying response?

answers.text: Restore the parts that worked and try again.
Find a way for the setback itself to become useful.
Secure what remains and adapt the plan.
Come back with something bigger and more ambitious.

questions.question: Put these projects in order from most interesting to least interesting.

answers.text: Build a team of creatures that becomes powerful together.
Create lasting magical effects that improve everything you do.
Connect inventions that give each other new abilities.
Expand your territory to produce more resources over time.

questions.question: How much do you enjoy responding to other people’s plans rather than focusing only on your own?
You have one free afternoon and a limited budget. Which sounds most rewarding?

answers.text: Spend it on one amazing experience right now.
Make a few smaller purchases or improvements that will last.
Keep some money aside in case plans change.
Save it toward a very specific dream purchase.

questions.question: Rank these endings from most satisfying to least satisfying.

answers.text: An army overwhelms the battlefield.
One legendary champion lands the final hit.
A clever combination wins suddenly.
I outlast everyone until they have no answers.

questions.question: You can give your allies one unusual ability. Which do you choose?

answers.text: Keep gaining permanent strength.
Disappear and return to reuse special abilities.
Create extra allies as you play.
Reward me for casting spells in succession.

questions.question: How much would you enjoy managing lots of abilities that interact with each other?
Your group has a problem that nobody can solve by the obvious method. What would you do?

answers.text: Borrow an idea or tool from someone who is doing well.
Figure out which parts of the problem can be removed.
Get other people on board to solve it together.
Find a completely different goal that makes the problem irrelevant.

questions.question: If you could win without attacking with creatures, how would you want to?

answers.text: Steal away their life while restoring mine.
Blast them with spells and direct damage.
Empty their library so they cannot draw a card.
Fulfill an unusual condition that says I win.

questions.question: How willing are you to risk progress you already made for the chance at a much bigger reward?
Pick up to two experiences you would love to have in a game.

answers.text: Feel powerful through creatures and combat.
Build a system that generates benefits turn after turn.
Predict and stop an opponent’s important move.
Pull off an unexpected combination.

questions.question: Something you have been working on is going badly, and you can make one meaningful change. What do you prioritize?

answers.text: Make one bold move to turn everything around immediately.
Recover the best parts and rebuild steadily.
Keep flexibility to respond to whatever goes wrong next.
Try a long-shot idea that could solve everything at once.

questions.question: Rank the armies you would most like to lead.

answers.text: One unstoppable hero
Several enormous monsters
Many small allies
A team that upgrades together

questions.question: How appealing is turning one creature into an almost unstoppable champion?
How appealing is controlling a huge army of smaller creatures?
A hobby you have been practicing is finally improving. What progress would feel best?

answers.text: Each skill you already have keeps getting stronger.
You can now do much more at once.
Your different skills work better together.
Your favorite skill becomes incredibly reliable.

questions.question: Which two themes would you actually want to see in your deck?

answers.text: Dragons and enormous beasts.
Spirits, ghosts, and creatures returning from death.
Constructs, robots, and inventions.
Wizards with weird magical abilities.

questions.question: You unexpectedly receive a generous gift card. What sounds most fun?

answers.text: Buy one big, impressive thing you have wanted.
Get lots of smaller things to enjoy together.
Upgrade something you already love.
Buy tools or supplies that make future projects easier.

questions.question: How satisfying would it be if every new member of your team strengthened the others?
How enjoyable would managing a crowded battlefield with many creatures and abilities be?
You can have one benefit that repeats each week. Which would you enjoy most?

answers.text: Something that keeps improving the environment around me.
A growing supply of resources for future plans.
Quietly reducing the options available to my competition.
Turning things I no longer need into useful rewards.

questions.question: How appealing is keeping track of +1/+1 counters and watching individual creatures develop?
Rank these ways of using creatures more than once.

answers.text: Bring them back after they die
Sacrifice them for rewards
Exile and return them to reuse abilities
Make copies of them

questions.question: How satisfying is having your own creatures die because it helps your strategy?
You discover a workshop with four different crafts. What would you learn?

answers.text: Build objects whose abilities depend on other objects.
Create magic that stays in place and changes the rules.
Chain spells together for growing effects.
Make creatures that produce useful effects when they arrive.

questions.question: How much would you enjoy several little effects triggering one after another?
Pick up to two resources you would be most excited to have in abundance.

answers.text: Extra life and recovery
More mana and lands
More cards to choose from
More creatures

questions.question: Halfway through a creative project, something goes wrong. Which backup would you prefer?

answers.text: Recover the original work you thought was lost.
Have spare materials ready to keep moving.
Turn the mistake into a useful new feature.
Change direction and make something else with what remains.

questions.question: How appealing is gaining life repeatedly while your other abilities do their jobs?
Rank these setbacks from MOST frustrating to LEAST frustrating.

answers.text: Losing the creatures I spent turns developing.
Running out of cards and useful choices.
Falling far behind in the first few turns.
Never finding the pieces my strategy depends on.

questions.question: What would you most like to be able to reuse as often as you want?

answers.text: My favorite creative techniques.
Projects I thought were finished or lost.
Resources that grow each time I expand my plans.
The special contributions of people I work with.

questions.question: How appealing is having a deck that behaves like a machine, with many interconnected pieces?
Rank these victories from most satisfying to least satisfying.

answers.text: Win through combat attacks.
Win by casting damaging magic directly.
Win by repeatedly draining life.
Win by emptying an opponent’s library.

questions.question: How satisfying is slowly wearing opponents down instead of winning all at once?
Someone else has a big advantage in a friendly competition. What sounds most satisfying?

answers.text: Figure out how to use the same advantage yourself.
Remove the advantage so things are more even.
Temporarily make the advantage irrelevant.
Focus on improving your own performance instead.

questions.question: How appealing is making opponents discard cards or lose access to options?
Which two surprising victory stories would you most want to experience?

answers.text: A series of effects combine into a winning loop.
I meet an unusual requirement that wins immediately.
My commander becomes the biggest threat on the table.
An enormous coordinated attack finishes everyone.

questions.question: A usual approach to a challenge stops working. What alternative would you try?

answers.text: Make your strongest existing approach even stronger.
Achieve small wins while maintaining your own energy.
Gradually reduce the other side’s future options.
Find a unique objective that bypasses the obstacle.

questions.question: How appealing is a card that lets you win by meeting a strange, specific condition?
Rank ways you would prefer to manage an opposing threat.

answers.text: Prevent it before it happens
Remove it after it appears
Steal it
Persuade another player to handle it

questions.question: Which behavior would you most want to discourage in a group game?

answers.text: Someone constantly targeting you.
Someone taking too many turns or actions in a row.
Someone accumulating advantages without sharing opportunities.
Someone crowding everyone else out of the activity.

questions.question: How fun would it be to play cards borrowed or stolen from your opponents?
Rank what would make completing a difficult challenge feel best.

answers.text: Finish before anyone expects me to.
Know my approach was dependable the whole time.
Pull off a clever solution that took planning.
Persevere through setbacks and finally succeed.

questions.question: How comfortable are you with turns involving lots of decisions and triggered abilities?
You can invest in one long-term personal project. Which approach sounds most rewarding?

answers.text: Make dependable progress through a repeatable routine.
Build layers of lasting improvements on what you have.
Expand resources so bigger projects become possible.
Turn things you no longer need into fuel for the next step.

questions.question: How frustrating is it when a deck needs several turns before it can do much?
Pick the two moments you would most look forward to.

answers.text: Landing a decisive attack.
Getting a complicated system to work.
Responding perfectly to an opponent’s move.
Discovering a strange combination.

questions.question: You and a friend are organizing an event together. How would you prefer to collaborate?

answers.text: Team up immediately if we want the same outcome.
Agree on exactly what each of us will handle.
Work independently and combine our work at the end.
Change roles depending on who needs the most help.

questions.question: How important is it to recover quickly after losing your main strategy?
Rank the qualities that make a deck appealing to you.

answers.text: A straightforward strategy that is easy to operate.
Lots of technical choices and intricate decisions.
Wild swings and unpredictable outcomes.
Reliable plans with opportunities to adapt.

questions.question: Which kind of hobby would you most enjoy getting better at?

answers.text: One where practice leads to reliable, repeatable progress.
One where you can try many different approaches.
One where unexpected surprises keep things interesting.
One where timing and reading other people matter most.

questions.question: How much do you enjoy choosing when to act based on what other players do?
In a group activity, which role sounds most fun?

answers.text: Take the lead and be the person everyone notices.
Quietly work toward a surprise reveal.
Bring everyone together and help people cooperate.
Keep things organized and step in when problems appear.

questions.question: How appealing is a strategy that sometimes does very little before one huge payoff?
How appealing is a deck whose best plays depend on what your opponents have?
questions.left: I want my own game plan

questions.question: How much would you enjoy making many small decisions each turn rather than one or two big decisions?
When learning a new activity, which would frustrate you most?

answers.text: Feeling like my efforts barely have an impact.
Having to redo progress I already made.
Trying to remember too many rules at once.
Waiting too long before I get to do anything fun.
